nodes.summary: For a function $g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, write $\partial_i g$ for its partial derivative along the $i$-th coordinate axis. If $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is twice continuously differentiable, then for all coordinate indices $i, j$ and every point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $\partial_j (\partial_i f)(x) = \partial_i (\partial_j f)(x)$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of mixed partial derivatives (Clairaut's theorem)

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the partial derivative $\partial_i f$ of $f$ along the $i$-th coordinate axis is the function $x \mapsto Df(x)\,e_i$, where $Df(x)$ is the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$.
nodes.title: Partial derivative function of a differentiable function

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at a point $x$, and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the partial derivative of $f$ along the $i$-th coordinate axis at $x$ equals $Df(x)\,e_i$, the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ applied to $e_i$.
nodes.title: Partial derivative as a Fréchet derivative

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable, write $e_k$ for the $k$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\partial_k g$ for the partial derivative of a function $g$ along the $k$-th coordinate axis, and let $Df$ be the Fréchet derivative of $f$, a map from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to the linear maps $\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$. nodes.title: Mixed partial derivatives via the second Fréchet derivative

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, a coordinate index $i$ and a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector. The partial derivative of $f$ along the $i$-th coordinate axis at $x$ equals the derivative at $t = 0$ of the one-variable function $t \mapsto f(x + t e_i)$, taken to be $0$ when that function is not differentiable at $0$.
nodes.title: Partial derivative as the derivative of a coordinate slice

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a coordinate index $i$, let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector. The partial derivative $\partial_i f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ sends $x$ to the derivative at $t = 0$ of $t \mapsto f(x + t e_i)$, taken to be $0$ when this function is not differentiable at $0$.
